info.title: sofabaton-x-server
info.description:
REST + WebSocket over the sofabaton-x library for Sofabaton X1 / X1S / X2 hubs. LAN service. Reads and control calls are free; once the admin account exists, every other write needs a token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-Sofabaton-Token) made in the control panel.

WebSocket: `/api/v1/events` (optional `?hub_id=` filter, repeatable) streams WsHello once, then WsHubEvent / WsServerEvent / WsJobEvent / WsPress / WsDropped messages (see components).

get.summary: Fresh read of one device's power state
get.description:
A hub round-trip on purpose: the device list is re-read (the
protocol's only read of the power byte), then the one row is
projected. ``power_state`` is 0 off / 1 on, or null when the row
carried no parseable record; a power macro commits the byte with a
short lag, so a caller that just fired must not expect an immediate
flip. A read the hub never answers is a 504, not a null.

Accepted.title: Accepted
Accepted.description: Result of a control call: the hub took it (True) or refused it.

Activity.title: Activity
Activity.description:
One activity from the hub's catalog.

``sort`` is the hub's stored display position (the byte the app's and
:meth:`AsyncXProxy.reorder_activities` writes set), ``0`` when the
record carries none. ``activities()`` already lists in that order.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: devices[] elements this activity edit touched (e.g. a new input entry); optional

ActivityPayload.title: ActivityPayload
ActivityPayload.description:
An edited activity element, plus the device elements the edit touched.

An activity edit can reach into a device: picking an input for a
device in the power-on sequence appends to that device's
``input_record``. ``devices`` carries those ``devices[]`` elements;
they are spliced into the edited bundle next to the activity and the
planner's scope guard decides what is allowed (input records, the
idle byte, command names).

ApplySummary.title: ApplySummary
ApplySummary.description: One apply record as ``GET /applies`` lists it (documents omitted).

ApplyView.title: ApplyView
ApplyView.description: The full record: the summary plus every item and the two documents.

AuthInfo.title: AuthInfo
AuthInfo.description: Whether writes need a credential: false until the admin account exists.

AuthStatus.title: AuthStatus
AuthStatus.description: ``GET /auth``: whether access is set up and who this request is.

BindRequest.title: BindRequest
BindRequest.description: Bind a button: the command, and optionally a different one for the held press.

Button.title: Button
Button.description:
A remote button bound on an activity or device.

``button_code`` is what you send to that entity; ``device_id`` /
``command_id`` are the underlying target it maps to, None for an
unbound slot. ``name`` is the ``ButtonName`` alias when the code has
one. ``long_press_device_id`` / ``long_press_command_id`` are the
hub's long-press binding for the same button, both None when the
button has none; the remote hardware fires it on a hold, and a
client that wants the same gesture sends the pair with ``send()``
(there is no long-press send, the pair is an ordinary command).

power_on_slot.title: Power On Slot
power_on_slot.description: slot the hub fires when an activity powers on (X1S/X2)

CallbackDeviceRequest.title: CallbackDeviceRequest
CallbackDeviceRequest.description:
Complete desired spec for POST and PUT, not a partial update.

Every slot is written; omitted slots become ``Button n`` and omitted
power/input hooks are cleared. For a rename, copy all fields from the
current record's spec and change only the intended labels. Preserving
device/command IDs and generic bindings does not preserve omitted fields.
Hook slots are one-based (1..10); callback URL indexes are zero-based (0..9).

target.description: null for an mqtt device: it calls no address

key.title: Key
key.description: the record's key under /wifi-devices; the callback device is 'default'

transport.title: Transport
transport.description: how its presses reach the server: http or mqtt

mqtt_topic.title: Mqtt Topic
mqtt_topic.description: an mqtt device's press topic on the broker, `<MAC>/up`

CallbackDeviceView.title: CallbackDeviceView
CallbackDeviceView.description:
The deployed record plus the destination a new deploy would use now.

``target`` is the address already written to the device;
``effective_destination`` follows current settings and can differ.
``stale`` flags a missing device; ``callback_device_stale`` is an event/error name.

button.title: Button
button.description: hub button code bound to this command in each of `activities`

long_press.title: Long Press
long_press.description: also bind the slot's long record to that button's long press

activities.title: Activities
activities.description: activity ids; kept only while `favorite` or `button` is set

input_activity_id.title: Input Activity Id
input_activity_id.description: the activity whose start performs this command (X1S/X2)

CallbackSlot.title: CallbackSlot
CallbackSlot.description:
One command slot: its labels and, optionally, where its command goes.

``favorite`` and ``button`` apply in every activity of ``activities``;
an update writes them in place and later removes only what an earlier
spec put there. One slot per button and one slot per input activity.

Command.title: Command
Command.description: A device command; send with ``send(device_id, command_id)``.

remember.title: Remember
remember.description: keep the session across browser restarts (90 days, renewed with use)

Device.title: Device
Device.description:
One device from the hub's catalog.

``power_state`` is the hub's live power byte for the device (0 off,
1 on) as of the last devices fetch; None when the row carried no
parseable record. The hub commits it with a macro-runtime lag after a
power fire, so it is not an instantaneous read. ``idle_behavior`` is
the device's power-behaviour mode when known. ``sort`` is the hub's
stored display position (what :meth:`AsyncXProxy.reorder_devices`
writes), ``0`` when the record carries none; ``devices()`` already
lists in that order.

device_class.title: Device Class
device_class.description: Protocol class: X1 supports ir, wifi_roku, wifi_hue, wifi_sonos; X1S also supports wifi_ip; X2 also supports wifi_mqtt. This is not an appliance category such as TV or receiver.

DevicePowerState.title: DevicePowerState
DevicePowerState.description: ``GET /hubs/{id}/devices/{did}/power-state``: a fresh read of one power byte.

EffectiveDestination.title: EffectiveDestination
EffectiveDestination.description: What a deploy would bake into the records right now (settings, else the routed local IP).

EntityIdentity.title: EntityIdentity
EntityIdentity.description: The ``device`` block of an entity payload: id and name are typed, the rest rides along.

EntityPayload.title: EntityPayload
EntityPayload.description:
An edited ``activities[]`` / ``devices[]`` element of the snapshot document.

Only ``device.device_id`` is checked here (it must match the path);
the tables are the library's ``hub_bundle`` rows. The planner refuses
anything outside the entity being edited, and a changed name must fit
the hub's name slot; the rest of the rows are not validated the way
the HA editor validates them.

Favorite.title: Favorite
Favorite.description: An activity favorite: a device command; send with ``send(device_id, command_id)``.

HubConfig.title: HubConfig
HubConfig.description:
Everything needed to proxy one hub, as data.

Fields beyond ``host`` refine the proxy's mDNS identity (``name``,
``txt``, ``hub_version``) or its two network faces (``port`` on the
hub, ``hub_listen_port`` and ``app_discovery_port`` on this host).
``is_proxy`` is True when the record was built from one of *our own*
proxy advertisements rather than a physical hub; a consumer
registering hubs from a foreign discovery feed uses it to map such a
record back to the hub it already fronts instead of proxying a proxy.

HubCreate.title: HubCreate
HubCreate.description: Body of ``POST /hubs``: the ``HubConfig`` fields, host required.

HubInfo.title: HubInfo
HubInfo.description:
Identity of the physical hub, as read from its connect banner.

``known`` is False until the banner has been read at least once; the
other fields are then None. The ``firmware_*`` verdicts are the
library's floors (:mod:`hub_versions`) applied to the reported
version, the same ones :class:`HubStatus` carries.

HubStatus.title: HubStatus
HubStatus.description: Live connection state of one proxied hub. Pure state read, no hub traffic.

HubStatusView.title: HubStatusView
HubStatusView.description: ``GET /hubs/{id}/status``: the server's enabled flag beside the library status.

HubSyncItemView.title: HubSyncItemView
HubSyncItemView.description: One unit of a document write, in run order.

HubSyncPlanView.title: HubSyncPlanView
HubSyncPlanView.description:
What ``PUT /snapshot`` would do, in order. Nothing is written.

``live_check`` lists the entities re-read before the first write;
``provisional_ids`` maps each placeholder to the id the preview
assumed (the hub assigns the real one). ``notes`` are the things a
UI may want to confirm first: deletions, payload overwrites,
membership changes.

HubView.title: HubView
HubView.description:
What ``/hubs`` returns per hub: the record, a status snapshot and
the hub's jobs (``active_job``: the one queued or running now;
``last_job``: the newest finished one, whatever its outcome), so a
client rebuilds "what is this hub doing" from the one list call
(server panel state plan, decision 1). ``hub_name`` is the hub's own
name from its banner, for display when ``config.name`` is not set.

JobView.title: JobView
JobView.description: One job as the API shows it.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: seconds to wait for a key press

Macro.title: Macro
Macro.description: An activity macro; send with ``send(activity_id, command_id)``.

MqttConfigBody.title: MqttConfigBody
MqttConfigBody.description:
The broker. Leave ``password`` out to keep the stored one (only while the
destination stays the same); send it empty or null to remove it.

source.title: Source
source.description: none: no broker; panel: stored by the control panel (mqtt.json); startup: set by command-line flags or environment variables, read-only here

editable.title: Editable
editable.description: false when the command line or the environment set the broker

port.title: Port
port.description: as configured; null = the default for the TLS choice

tls_ca.title: Tls Ca
tls_ca.description: a CA certificate file on the server's host

devices_using.title: Devices Using
devices_using.description: Wifi Devices on the mqtt transport, across hubs

password_dropped.title: Password Dropped
password_dropped.description: this change moved the destination without a new password, so the stored password was dropped

MqttConfigView.title: MqttConfigView
MqttConfigView.description: The broker settings, never the password.

MqttView.title: MqttView
MqttView.description:
The server's broker connection. The settings come from the command line or the
environment, or else from the control panel (PUT /server/mqtt/config); the password
is not part of any answer. ``wanted`` is true while a device uses the transport; the
connection exists only then.

command_id.title: Command Id
command_id.description: a free slot; omitted = the next free one

order.title: Order
order.description: every entity of the kind, once, in display order

value.title: Value
value.description: in effect now (a change applies at once, no restart)

pinned.title: Pinned
pinned.description: set by an environment variable or CLI flag; server.json cannot change it

OriginsSetting.title: OriginsSetting
OriginsSetting.description: The browser origins on another host or port that get CORS and pass the Origin guard.

PayloadSpec.title: PayloadSpec
PayloadSpec.description:
One IR payload in any supported source format (exactly one field).

``hex``: the hub's stored body as hex; ``pronto``: a learned-format
Pronto code; ``timings_us`` + ``carrier_hz``: raw mark/space durations
in microseconds, mark first; ``descriptor``: a protocol line such as
``P:NEC1 D:4 S:5 F:21``.

PayloadView.title: PayloadView
PayloadView.description:
A stored payload: its kind, the hub body as hex, and what could be read from it.

``kind`` follows the library's payload types: ``raw`` or
``descriptive`` for an IR payload, ``network`` for a decoded network
command (``wifi_ip`` / ``wifi_roku`` / ``wifi_hue`` / ``wifi_sonos``)
and ``record`` for any other stored body (a Bluetooth key, a two-byte
``wifi_mqtt`` record, an undecodable network body). Only IR payloads
can be fired with ``POST /play``. ``decoded`` is the library's
structured block for the payloads that have one (a descriptive IR
payload, a network command, a ``wifi_mqtt`` record):
``{"class", "fields", "trailer_hex"}`` as ``restore_data.decoded``
carries it; null when the body stays raw.

configured.title: Configured
configured.description: the value the next start uses (pinned, else server.json, else the default)

pinned.title: Pinned
pinned.description: set by an environment variable or CLI flag; server.json cannot change it

PortSetting.title: PortSetting
PortSetting.description: One port: what runs now, what the next start will use, and where from.

PressPage.title: PressPage
PressPage.description:
``GET /hubs/{id}/presses``: the ring, oldest first when ``after`` is given.

``expired`` means presses newer than ``after`` were already evicted
from the ring; the client missed some and must accept the gap.
``instance_id`` changes on every server restart, and so does the
sequence; on a new instance start from the current ``hello``.

device_key.title: Device Key
device_key.description: the Wifi Device's key; null for an unknown device

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: Error body (RFC 9457 shape, minus the URI scheme).

RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest
RefreshRequest.description: Body of ``POST /hubs/{id}/snapshot/refresh``: one entity, or neither for the whole hub.

document.title: Document
document.description: the remote card's configuration keys (the HA card's YAML as JSON, minus entity, theme and Home Assistant actions); an empty object resets to defaults

bundle.title: Bundle
bundle.description: a full hub_bundle from POST /backup (payload_profile full_backup)

RunningActivity.title: RunningActivity
RunningActivity.description: The activity currently running on the hub.

SeenHub.title: SeenHub
SeenHub.description: A physical hub advertised on the LAN (not yet necessarily configured).

command_id.title: Command Id
command_id.description: command id, macro id, or button code

ServerInfo.title: ServerInfo
ServerInfo.description: What ``GET /api/v1/server`` returns (and what the mDNS TXT says, in full).

allowed_origins.title: Allowed Origins
allowed_origins.description: exact origins such as http://nas:8123 (no path, no wildcard); an empty list removes them all

ServerSettingsUpdate.title: ServerSettingsUpdate
ServerSettingsUpdate.description: Body of ``PUT /server/settings``; omitted ports are left as they are.

SnapshotDocument.title: SnapshotDocument
SnapshotDocument.description:
``GET /hubs/{id}/snapshot``: the structural configuration plus its header.

The body is the library's ``hub_bundle`` with the snapshot header
merged in. Send the quoted ``snapshot_id`` as ``If-Match`` for edits.
The response ``ETag`` is a distinct, opaque conditional-read validator
that also covers provenance; send it unchanged as ``If-None-Match``.

SnapshotEditDocument.title: SnapshotEditDocument
SnapshotEditDocument.description:
The edited snapshot document: what ``GET /snapshot`` returned, changed.

Header fields are ignored (``snapshot_id`` goes in ``If-Match``). A new
device or activity carries a negative ``device.device_id`` of the
client's choosing, and every reference to it elsewhere in the document
(bindings, favorites, macro steps, membership) uses that same negative
id; the hub assigns the real id and the server maps it. The array
order of ``devices`` / ``activities`` is the display order. A removed
entity must be removed from every activity in the same document.

SnapshotEntityPayload.title: SnapshotEntityPayload
SnapshotEntityPayload.description:
One device or activity in the snapshot: provenance typed, tables open.

``complete`` / ``editable`` / ``fetched_at`` are the library's
per-entity provenance (facts about the server's copy, never about
the hub); ``commands``, ``button_bindings``,
``macros``, ``favorite_slots`` and the other tables follow the
library's ``hub_bundle`` shape and are passed through as they are.

SyncPlan.title: SyncPlan
SyncPlan.description: What a sync of this edit would write, in order. Nothing is written.

name.title: Name
name.description: what the token is for, e.g. the integration's name

TokenCreated.title: TokenCreated
TokenCreated.description: The new token; ``token`` is the secret and is never shown again.

TokenInfo.title: TokenInfo
TokenInfo.description: A write token as the panel lists it; the secret is never kept.

UpdateStatus.title: UpdateStatus
UpdateStatus.description:
What ``GET /server/updates`` (and the ``update`` block of ``GET /server``) says.

``status`` is the verdict of the last check against the version running
now: ``not_checked`` (none on record), ``up_to_date`` (the last check
found nothing newer), ``update_available`` (``latest_version`` is
newer), ``failed`` (the last check did not get an answer; ``error``
says why, and nothing is known about newer releases).

WifiDeviceList.title: WifiDeviceList
WifiDeviceList.description:
``GET /hubs/{id}/wifi-devices``: every managed Wifi Device of the hub,
the callback device (key ``default``) first.

power_on_slot.title: Power On Slot
power_on_slot.description: slot the hub fires when an activity powers on (X1S/X2)

WifiDeviceRequest.title: WifiDeviceRequest
WifiDeviceRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /wifi-devices``: the callback device's spec plus the transport.

``PUT /wifi-devices/{key}`` takes the same body; the transport of a
deployed device is fixed and the field is ignored there. ``mqtt``
needs an X2 and a server with a broker (set in the control panel, or ``--mqtt-host``): the
hub then publishes the presses to the broker set in the Sofabaton
app, no listener and no callback address involved.

WriteProgress.title: WriteProgress
WriteProgress.description:
One progress report from a long-running operation (refresh, sync).

``phase`` is the operation's own phase word (``preparing``, ``device``,
``activity``, ``stale_check``, ``writing``, ``reading_back``,
``finalizing`` ...);
``entity_kind`` / ``entity_id`` name the entity being worked on when
there is one; ``step_kind`` is the sync step kind while writing.

ActivityChanged.description: The running activity changed (None = powered off / idle).
ActivityChanged.title: ActivityChanged

CatalogReady.description: The connect-time initial sync completed (True) or the session dropped (False).
CatalogReady.title: CatalogReady

ConnectionState.description: A hub-side (``hub_state``) or app-side (``app_state``) link came up or went down.
ConnectionState.title: ConnectionState

SnapshotChanged.description:
The snapshot projection moved: a refresh landed, a write was rebased,
or the cache was imported.

``device_ids`` / ``activity_ids`` name the entities the emitting
operation touched (empty when the whole cache is meant, as after an
import).
SnapshotChanged.title: SnapshotChanged

StatusChanged.description: The proxy's mode flipped (derived from hub and app connection state).
StatusChanged.title: StatusChanged

WsServerEvent.description:
A server lifecycle event. ``hub_id`` is empty for a server-wide kind
(``update_check``); a ``?hub_id=`` filter never receives those.
WsServerEvent.title: WsServerEvent

WsPress.description:
A button press the hub delivered to the callback listener.

``seq`` is the server-instance press sequence shared with
``GET /hubs/{id}/presses`` (de-duplicate across the two channels by
it; resume with ``?after=``). ``resolution`` says how the press was
matched to the callback device: ``deployed`` (label from the record),
``stale`` (the record is flagged stale), ``unknown_slot`` (outside the
record), ``unknown_device`` (no record for that device id).
WsPress.title: WsPress

bearerAuth.description: A write token (sbx_...) made in the control panel under Server settings > Access.

tokenHeader.name: X-Sofabaton-Token
tokenHeader.description: The same token, for clients whose Authorization header belongs to a reverse proxy's own auth.

sessionCookie.name: sbx_session_<install id>
sessionCookie.description: The control panel's sign-in (POST /auth/login); the name carries the server's install id.
